method: Wilson score interval with z=1.96. Normal half-widths use 1.96 * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n) and are approximations. Hypothetical rows are not measurements.

observed.name: phase35_unseen_luxury
observed.interpretation: The interval stays above 0.80. This is substantial warning evidence. It is not a final multi-source benchmark.

observed.name: phase35_watch_like
observed.interpretation: Groups C, D, and E together. The interval stays near 0.79 to 0.88.

observed.name: phase35_rolex
observed.interpretation: Rolex dominates the unseen-luxury sample. A Rolex rate is not a four-brand rate.

observed.name: phase36_unseen_holdout
observed.interpretation: Width is about 0.40. The pre-registered minimum was 60. This observation cannot confirm or overturn Phase 35.

observed.name: phase36_ordinary_holdout
observed.interpretation: The interval includes both a large drop and a majority-escape result. Minimum was 40.

observed.name: phase36_overall_holdout
observed.interpretation: Underpowered. Not a safety result and not a confirmation of the Phase 35 rate.

hypothetical_intervals.name: n60_if_escape_were_0.05
hypothetical_intervals.role: Shows why 60 can separate a near-0.05 safety claim from a 0.50 failure.

hypothetical_intervals.name: n60_if_escape_were_0.50
hypothetical_intervals.role: The lower bound stays above the upper bound of the 0.05 row. The two claims do not share a 95 percent interval at n=60.

hypothetical_intervals.name: n14_if_escape_were_0
hypothetical_intervals.role: Even a perfect 14-image result would have an upper bound above 0.20. Phase 36 did not observe zero escapes.

hypothetical_intervals.name: n8_brand_normal_half_width_at_0.50
hypothetical_intervals.role: Eight images stop an empty brand from being reported. They do not estimate a brand rate precisely.

what_each_minimum_protects.holdout_unseen_luxury_60: Stops a 14-image interval of width 0.40 from being treated as a conclusion. At n=60, a 0.05 rate and a 0.50 rate have non-overlapping Wilson intervals.
what_each_minimum_protects.holdout_ordinary_40: Phase 35 ordinary evidence was 22 images and Phase 36 was 10. Forty images bring a 0.50-rate normal half-width to about 0.155.
what_each_minimum_protects.holdout_smart_digital_25: Phase 36 had 1 image. Twenty-five images block a single-photo anecdote. The normal half-width at 0.50 is still about 0.196, so this is a floor, not a precise rate.
what_each_minimum_protects.holdout_wrist_store_25: Phase 36 had 0 and Phase 35 had 18. The frozen protocol says a wrist shortfall alone does not block a conclusion. Twenty-five remains the useful floor for a wrist claim.
what_each_minimum_protects.four_brands_with_8: Phase 35 unseen luxury was 180 Rolex images out of 194. Four brands block a one-brand result. Eight images per brand block an empty cell. Neither number is a precise brand-rate study.
what_each_minimum_protects.max_single_brand_fraction_0.4: Stops a holdout that is mostly one brand from being described as a multi-brand result.
what_each_minimum_protects.collection_targets_300_200_100_50: Headroom for splits, brand caps, and content rejections. They are governance and diversity targets above the holdout floors. Missing them blocked Phase 37. Lowering them was not done.
